contributions.headingText: Sarcomatoid carcinoma is a primary thymic carcinoma partly or completely composed of spindle-shaped epithelial cells. Tumours with heterologous sarcomatous elements are called carcinosarcomas.
2C27.0 & XH35M3 Carcinoma of thymus & Pseudosarcomatous carcinoma
Acceptable: spindle cell or metaplastic carcinoma; carcinosarcoma.
Sarcomatoid carcinoma of the thymus is localized in the anterior (prevascular) mediastinum.

The commonest symptoms include chest pain, cough, shortness of breath, and superior vena cava syndrome [[Travis WD, Brambilla E, Burke AP, et al., editors. WHO classification of tumours of the lung, pleura, thymus and heart. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2015. (WHO classification of tumours series, 4th ed.; vol. 7). https://publications.iarc.fr/17.]]. No autoimmune diseases are reported in the International Thymic Malignancy Interest Group (ITMIG) cohort {25524678}.

Imaging

The tumours, large and lobular, usually show poorly defined borders. Areas of low attenuation on CT correlate with necrotic areas {9103218; 20034984}. Extensive local invasion occurs {27847081}. Metastases to regional lymph nodes and lung are common.

Sarcomatoid carcinoma accounts for 2.5–10% of all thymic carcinomas, occurring mostly in the fourth to eighth decades of life. In the ITMIG cohort, 18 of 6097 patients with thymic epithelial neoplasm (including 706 patients with thymic carcinomas) have sarcomatoid carcinoma. The average age is 47 years {25524678}.

A subset of sarcomatoid carcinomas co-occur with type A thymoma, metaplastic thymoma, other thymic carcinomas, or multilocular thymic cysts, from which they may arise {10366152; 16711401; 22706865; 21677542}. In other cases the etiology is unknown.
One case of sarcomatoid carcinoma has been reported that showed a complex chromosomal abnormality including der(16)t(1:16)(q12;q12.1), similar to a case of thymic squamous cell carcinoma {11903597}.

The tumours are often large, with infiltrative borders. The fleshy white or grey cut surfaces often show areas of haemorrhage, necrosis, and cystic degeneration [[Travis WD, Brambilla E, Burke AP, et al., editors. WHO classification of tumours of the lung, pleura, thymus and heart. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2015. (WHO classification of tumours series, 4th ed.; vol. 7). https://publications.iarc.fr/17.]].

Tumours may consist entirely of malignant spindle cells with moderately to highly atypical features, arranged in fascicles or storiform arrays {10366152}. They are mitotically active {22706865}. Some cases are admixed with type A thymoma {10366152} or metaplastic thymoma {20034984} or have a rhabdomyomatous component {30217623}.

In sarcomatoid transformation of thymic carcinoma, both malignant epithelial (carcinomatous) and spindle cell (sarcomatous/sarcomatoid) components may occur {1991250}. Tumours with heterologous mesenchymal elements such as rhabdomyosarcoma, osteosarcoma, or chondrosarcoma (carcinosarcoma) may occur [[Travis WD, Brambilla E, Burke AP, et al., editors. WHO classification of tumours of the lung, pleura, thymus and heart. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2015. (WHO classification of tumours series, 4th ed.; vol. 7). https://publications.iarc.fr/17.]]. In some cases, the epithelial nature of the tumour can be demonstrated only by immunohistochemistry or electron microscopy {11903597}.

Differential diagnosis

Atypical type A thymoma usually shows low-grade nuclear atypia, is CD5-negative, and may harbour rare TdT-positive immature T cells {27926794}. Metaplastic thymoma is a biphasic tumour with consistently bland, mitotically inactive spindle cells; variably atypical epithelial islands; and common YAP1-MAML2 gene fusion {31641231}.

Thymic neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) with spindle cell features are distinguished by a prominent vasculature and synaptophysin and/or chromogranin expression {10392634; 31042566}.

Other biphasic tumours, such as mesothelioma, synovial sarcoma, or metastases may require appropriate ancillary studies for recognition.
Atypical spindle cells in smears can hint to thymic sarcomatoid carcinoma {18514125}.

Essential:

  • A thymic epithelial carcinoma either partly or completely composed of atypical spindle cells with at least focal epithelial features; carcinosarcoma includes heterologous sarcomatous elements

Desirable:

  • Epithelial components may stain with characteristic markers

Sarcomatoid carcinomas should be staged according to the TNM system [[Brierley JD, Gospodarowicz MK, Wittekind C, editors. TNM classification of malignant tumours. 8th ed. Oxford (UK): Wiley-Blackwell; 2017.]] {25396314} and, optionally, the Masaoka–Koga system {21847052}. In the ITMIG cohort, 17% of sarcomatoid carcinomas are in stage I/II, 33% in stage III, and 50% in stage IV {25524678}.
This tumour type is highly aggressive. In the ITMIG cohort, the survival and outcome indicators are similar to those for other thymic carcinoma types {25524678}.
